title: Why do footballers wear “bras”? Meet the GPS vest
description: That short black top on a footballer usually holds a tracking device. Discover what GPS vests measure and why the fabric is only part of the story.

cover.alt: A footballer seen from behind wears a black tracking vest over a grey shirt, with a small pod in an upper-back pocket beside a green pitch

sections.title: The top under the shirt
sections.html:
The short black top often mistaken for a bra on male footballers is usually a GPS tracking vest. It holds a small electronic device used to measure the player’s movement.

You may spot one when a player swaps shirts. Tracking-equipment maker STATSports explains the vest’s purpose. For soccer fans wondering about the unfamiliar outfit, the answer is wearable technology.

sections.title: The cloth is not the tracker
sections.html:
The garment keeps the monitoring pod in place while the player runs and turns. STATSports’ vest description separates the fabric vest from the tracker and shows the pocket on the upper back.

The vest can be worn over or under a training top. It is a practical holder for the hardware, rather than a shirt that somehow knows the score.

sections.title: Turning running into numbers
sections.html:
FIFA’s tracking-system overview describes measures such as distance covered and running speed. Those numbers help staff examine the physical work behind a performance.

A long sprint and a gentle jog tell different stories. Movement data adds detail to what coaches see; it does not turn effort into an automatic goal, tackle or match-winning pass.

sections.title: GPS is one way to track play
sections.html:
FIFA also describes local-positioning wearables and camera-based tracking. A running statistic does not necessarily come from a GPS vest, and equipment varies between systems.
